summary: Jampa Mackenzie Stewart is a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He studied under traditional teachers Khenpo Karthar Rinpoche and Jamgon Kongtrul Rinpoche.

Jampa Samten specializes in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. His career includes serving as Director (attested 2015) and later as a re-employed Professor (attested 2026) at the Central Institute of Higher Tibetan Studies.

Jamphel Yeshe Gyaltsen (1912–1947) worked in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He studied under the 13th Dalai Lama, Kalu Rinpoche, Chatral Sangye Dorje, and Tsennyi Tulku Jampal Norbu, and he taught the 14th Dalai Lama and the 19th Kushok Bakula Rinpoche.

Jamyang Khyentse Wangpo (1820–1892) was a scholar in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He studied under numerous teachers, including Minling Khenchen Rigdzin Zangpo, Jamgön Kongtrul Lodrö Thayé, and Chokgyur Lingpa, and taught Jamgön Ju Mipham Gyatso, Jamgön Kongtrul, and others.
Jamyang Sherab Chokyi Nangwa studied under Jamgön Kongtrul Lodrö Thayé and Jamyang Khyentse Wangpo.

Jan Chozen Bays (b. 1945) works in Buddhist and religious studies. She studied at Swarthmore College, UC San Diego, and under Hakuyu Taizan Maezumi and Shōdō Harada. She taught at Zen Community of Oregon and became abbess of Great Vow Zen Monastery.

Jan Christian Schaffert works in Indology and computational studies. Attested in 2026, he studied as a Bearbeiter and served as a project collaborator (Mitarbeiter) on the EdiKILex project at the Göttingen Academy of Sciences and Humanities.
Jan Dolensky is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He earned his Magister der Philosophie at the University of Vienna, attested in 2013, under the supervision of Klaus-Dieter Mathes.

Jan Fontein (1927–2017) specialized in Buddhist studies and art history. He earned his PhD at Leiden University under Theodoor Paul Galestin and served as curator at the Rijksmuseum and the Museum of Fine Arts, Boston.

Jan Gonda (1905–1991) was an Indologist and linguist. He earned his PhD at Utrecht University and also studied at Leiden University. He held the Chair of Sanskrit (from 1929) and was Professor of Indology (1932–1976) at Utrecht University.

Jan Jakob Maria de Groot (1854–1921) was a scholar of Sinology and religious studies who studied at Leiden University and under Georg von der Gabelentz. He served as a professor at Leiden University and Humboldt University of Berlin.
Jan Jaworski (1903–1945) was a scholar of Sinology, Japanology, and Buddhist studies. He studied at the University of Warsaw and under Stanisław Schayer and Jean Przyluski.

Jan Julius Lodewijk Duyvendak (1889–1954) was a Sinologist who studied at Leiden University, the University of Paris, and Humboldt University of Berlin. He was a lecturer and then Professor of Chinese Language and Literature at Leiden University.

Jan N. Bremmer (b. 1944) works in religious studies and history. He completed doctorates after studies at Vrije Universiteit Amsterdam and the University of Amsterdam, and held posts including Assistant Professor at Utrecht University and Chair of Religious Studies at Groningen.

Jan Nattier (b. 1949) specializes in Buddhist studies, Sinology, and Central Asian studies. She studied at Indiana and Harvard universities, and held professorial posts at Indiana University Bloomington and the International Research Institute for Advanced Buddhology at Soka University.

Jan P. Hogendijk (b. 1955) specializes in the history of science and Central Asian studies. After completing his doctorate at Utrecht University, he held posts as Professor of the History of Mathematics at Utrecht University and Leiden University.

Jan Peter F. Hintelmann specializes in religious studies and Tibetology. He earned his PhD at the University of Hamburg under Marianne Pieper, and also studied under traditional teachers including Thubten Nyandak, Tenzin Kunga, Sonam Senge, and Geshe Sonam Rinchen.

Jan Van Bragt (1928–2007) worked in philosophy, Buddhist studies, and religious studies. After studying at KU Leuven, he served as a professor at Nanzan University (~1967–1998) and as Director of the Nanzan Institute for Religion and Culture (~1976–1990).

Jan Westerhoff (b. 1976) specializes in philosophy, Buddhist studies, and Indology. He earned degrees from the University of Cambridge and SOAS University of London, and serves as Professor of Buddhist Philosophy at the University of Oxford.

Jan Willem de Jong (1921–2000) was an Indologist and Tibetologist. He earned his PhD at Leiden University and held the Chair of Tibetan and Buddhist Studies there, later serving as Head of South Asian and Buddhist Studies at Australian National University.
